reason: The text depicts Moses and Aaron responding to rebellion, not initiating antagonism toward the Hebrew people. When Korah and 250 leaders challenge their authority, Moses proposes a fair test before God rather than acting punitively. When God executes the rebels, Moses and Aaron work to protect the people—Aaron specifically intercedes with incense to stop the plague that breaks out ('vaya'amod bein-hameitim u'vein-hachaim'—he stands between the dead and the living). The antagonism flows in the opposite direction: the people are antagonistic toward the leaders, as shown when 'the whole congregation of the children of Israel complained against Moses and Aaron' the next day ('vayillonu...al-Moshe v'al-Aharon'). The leaders' actions demonstrate protection of and intercession for the people, not antagonism toward them.
